events.title: Lucy
events.description: A partial skeleton found at Hadar in the Afar in 1974 shows an ancestor that walked upright with an ape-sized brain. In Ethiopia she is Dinkinesh, "you are marvellous".

events.title: The oldest stone tools at Gona
events.description: Flaked cobbles from the Afar are among the oldest known deliberately made tools. The Rift Valley keeps the deepest record of human ancestry anywhere.

events.title: Omo I, among the oldest modern humans
events.description: Skull fragments from the Kibish formation on the Omo River are among the earliest fossils of our own species.

events.title: Herto Man
events.description: Three skulls from the Middle Awash, one of them deliberately defleshed and polished, suggest mortuary practice among early modern humans.

events.title: Out of Africa across the Bab el-Mandeb
events.description: One leading reconstruction has the ancestors of most people outside Africa crossing from the Horn to Arabia across a narrowed southern Red Sea.

events.title: Teff and ensete are domesticated
events.description: The highlands domesticate crops grown nowhere else: teff, the grain of injera, and ensete, the false banana that still feeds millions in the south.

events.title: The land of Punt
events.description: Egyptian expeditions sail south for incense, ebony and live baboons. Punt lay somewhere on the southern Red Sea coast, and genetic work on mummified baboons points to the Eritrea and Ethiopia region.

events.title: The kingdom of D'mt
events.description: A kingdom in the northern highlands builds in dressed stone, uses irrigation and iron, and writes in a South Arabian script.

events.title: Beta Samati, a trading town
events.description: Excavations near Yeha uncover a town occupied for fourteen centuries across the shift from D'mt to Aksum, with a basilica, seals and a gold ring.

events.title: The temple at Yeha
events.description: A tall rectangular temple of fitted ashlar blocks, built in the style of Saba across the Red Sea, still stands. It is the oldest standing building in the country.

events.title: Ge'ez emerges
events.description: A Semitic language with its own script develops in the north. Ge'ez survives as the liturgical language of the Orthodox church long after it stopped being spoken.

events.title: Adulis in the Periplus
events.description: A Greek merchant's guide to the Red Sea names Adulis as the port of a king at Aksum, trading ivory, tortoiseshell and rhinoceros horn.

events.title: Aksum becomes a power
events.description: A highland kingdom grows rich on the trade between Rome, Arabia and India, and controls the routes from the interior to the Red Sea.

events.title: Aksum strikes its own coins
events.description: Aksum becomes one of the few states in the ancient world to issue gold coinage, minted in its kings' names with Greek legends for foreign trade.

events.title: The great stelae
events.description: Granite monoliths up to thirty-three metres tall are raised over royal tombs, carved to look like multi-storey houses. The tallest fell, perhaps as it was being erected.

events.title: Ezana converts to Christianity
events.description: Taught by a Syrian captive named Frumentius, King Ezana adopts Christianity and his coins swap the crescent and disc for a cross. Ethiopia is among the first Christian states.

events.title: Frumentius becomes the first bishop
events.description: Consecrated by Athanasius in Alexandria, he begins sixteen centuries in which the head of the Ethiopian church is an Egyptian monk.

events.title: Constantius writes to Ezana
events.description: The Roman emperor asks the king of Aksum to replace Frumentius with an Arian bishop. Athanasius preserves the letter, and there is no sign Aksum complied.

events.title: The Nine Saints
events.description: Monks from the eastern Mediterranean found monasteries and translate scripture into Ge'ez. Debre Damo, reached only by a rope up a cliff, is traditionally one of theirs.

events.title: Cosmas Indicopleustes at Aksum
events.description: A Greek merchant describes the king on a four-elephant chariot, the giraffes, and the gold trade conducted silently with the peoples of the south.

events.title: Kaleb invades Himyar
events.description: The Aksumite king crosses the Red Sea to avenge the massacre of Christians at Najran, and Aksum rules southern Arabia for half a century.

events.title: The first hijra
events.description: Followers of Muhammad, persecuted in Mecca, take refuge with the Christian king of Aksum, who refuses to hand them back. Islam reaches Africa as guests.

events.title: Aksum turns inland
events.description: The rise of the caliphate closes the Red Sea trade, Adulis declines, and the kingdom's centre drifts south into the highlands.

events.title: The legend of Queen Gudit
events.description: Tradition records a queen who sacks Aksum, burns its churches and hunts its royal family. Whoever she was, Aksumite power ends about now.

events.title: The Zagwe come to power
events.description: An Agaw dynasty from Lasta takes the throne. Later chroniclers call them usurpers because they could not claim descent from Solomon.

events.title: Yemrehana Krestos
events.description: A church of wood and stone built inside a cave mouth near Lalibela, in the Aksumite style, a century before the rock churches.

events.title: Islam spreads along the trade routes
events.description: Muslim sultanates grow on the routes inland from the Gulf of Aden, the Sultanate of Shewa among the first.

events.title: King Lalibela takes the throne
events.description: The most famous Zagwe king. Tradition says he was taken to heaven and shown a city to build on earth.

events.title: A chapel in Jerusalem
events.description: After Saladin takes Jerusalem the Ethiopian church is given rights at the Holy Sepulchre. Its monks still live on the roof, at Deir es-Sultan.

events.title: The rock churches of Lalibela
events.description: Eleven churches are carved downward out of the volcanic rock as single blocks, with trenches and tunnels between them, as a New Jerusalem for pilgrims who could not reach the old one.

events.title: Tekle Haymanot and the monasteries
events.description: A monk from Shewa founds Debre Libanos, which becomes the most powerful monastery in the kingdom and brokers the end of the Zagwe.

events.title: Yekuno Amlak restores the Solomonic line
events.description: A prince from Amhara overthrows the Zagwe and claims descent from Solomon and the Queen of Sheba. His line rules, with interruptions, until 1974.

events.title: The Kebra Nagast
events.description: The Glory of the Kings tells how Menelik, son of Solomon and Sheba, brought the Ark of the Covenant to Aksum. It becomes the founding text of the dynasty.

events.title: Amda Seyon defeats Ifat
events.description: The emperor campaigns against the Muslim sultanates to the east and makes them tributary. The highland kingdom roughly doubles.

events.title: The Adal Sultanate rises
events.description: After Ifat's defeat its ruling family regroups in the lowlands around Harar and founds Adal, the kingdom's great rival for a century.

events.title: Zara Yaqob reforms the church
events.description: A scholar emperor imposes doctrinal unity, Sabbath observance and a new capital at Debre Berhan, and writes theology himself.

events.title: Envoys at the Council of Florence
events.description: Ethiopian monks from Jerusalem attend the council in Italy, and Europe begins to connect the kingdom with the legend of Prester John.

events.title: Zara Yaqob defeats Adal at Gomit
events.description: The emperor routs the sultan's army and the sultan is killed. The Christian kingdom is at its height for the rest of the century.

events.title: Queen Eleni turns to Portugal
events.description: The regent writes to Lisbon proposing an alliance against the Muslim powers. Twenty years later it is needed.

events.title: Francisco Alvares at court
events.description: A Portuguese embassy spends six years with the moving royal camp. The chaplain's account is the first European eyewitness description of the kingdom.

events.title: Ahmad Gragn wins at Shimbra Kure
events.description: The imam of Adal, called Gragn, the left-handed, defeats the emperor's army. For fourteen years his forces overrun the highlands and burn churches and monasteries.

events.title: Four hundred Portuguese musketeers
events.description: Cristovao da Gama lands at Massawa with a small force to help Emperor Gelawdewos. He is captured and executed the next year.

events.title: Gragn falls at Wayna Daga
events.description: The imam is shot in battle near Lake Tana and his army disperses. The kingdom survives, exhausted.

events.title: The Oromo expansion
events.description: Oromo groups move north and east into the lands emptied by the wars, organised by the gadaa system of age grades. They become the country's largest people.

events.title: The Ottomans take Massawa
events.description: The Ottoman province of Habesh is founded on the coast, cutting the highlands off from the sea and from Portuguese help.

events.title: The walls of Harar
events.description: Emir Nur builds a wall round Harar after Adal's defeat. The walled city, with its eighty-two mosques, becomes a centre of Islamic learning in the Horn.

events.title: Susenyos converts to Catholicism
events.description: Persuaded by the Jesuit Pedro Paez, the emperor declares Catholicism the state religion. Years of civil war follow.

events.title: The Jesuits are expelled
events.description: Susenyos abdicates, his son Fasilides restores the Orthodox faith and expels the missionaries. Ethiopia closes to Europe for nearly two centuries.

events.title: Gondar becomes the capital
events.description: Fasilides builds a castle near Lake Tana and the court stops moving. The royal enclosure grows into a compound of stone palaces.

events.title: Zera Yacob's Hatata
events.description: A philosopher writes an inquiry into reason and faith, criticising all religions equally. Its authenticity was long disputed and is now widely accepted.

events.title: Iyasu II and Empress Mentewab
events.description: The empress rules with and then for her son, building churches at Gondar. Court politics fall into the hands of regional lords.

events.title: The murder of Iyoas
events.description: The warlord Ras Mikael Sehul has the emperor strangled. Emperors become puppets of rival nobles for eighty-six years, the Zemene Mesafint.

events.title: James Bruce at Gondar
events.description: A Scottish traveller reaches the source of the Blue Nile and returns with copies of the Book of Enoch, lost in Europe. He is disbelieved at home.

events.title: Coffee from Kaffa
events.description: The coffee plant originates in the southwestern forests of Kaffa, and wild coffee is still harvested there. Coffee ceremonies become part of daily life across the country.

events.title: Shewa grows strong in the south
events.description: Sahle Selassie makes the southern kingdom of Shewa the most orderly state in the highlands, receiving British and French envoys.

events.title: Richard Burton enters Harar
events.description: A British officer disguised as a Muslim merchant is the first European known to enter the city, then closed to outsiders. He stays ten days.

events.title: Tewodros II is crowned
events.description: Kassa Hailu, a bandit turned warlord, defeats the regional lords and has himself crowned. He sets out to rebuild a centralised empire with a modern army.

events.title: Magdala
events.description: A British expedition marches from the coast to free imprisoned envoys. Tewodros shoots himself rather than surrender, and the British loot the fortress library.

events.title: Yohannes IV
events.description: A Tigrayan ruler takes the throne and spends his reign fighting Egypt, Italy and the Sudanese Mahdists.

events.title: Egypt defeated at Gura
events.description: An Egyptian army led by European and American officers is routed in the Eritrean highlands, ending Khedive Ismail's plans for the interior.

events.title: Addis Ababa is founded
events.description: Empress Taytu chooses hot springs below Entoto for a new capital. The name means new flower.

events.title: Dogali
events.description: Ras Alula destroys an Italian column near Massawa. Rome sends a larger army.

events.title: The rinderpest famine
events.description: A cattle plague brought in with Italian livestock kills most of the herds, and drought and locusts follow. Perhaps a third of the population dies in four years.

events.title: Menelik II takes the throne
events.description: Yohannes dies fighting the Mahdists at Metemma and Menelik of Shewa becomes emperor.

events.title: The treaty of Wuchale
events.description: Its Amharic text lets Ethiopia use Italy for foreign relations; the Italian text says it must. Italy declares a protectorate on the strength of one verb.

events.title: Southern conquests
events.description: Menelik's armies push south and west, roughly doubling the empire and taking in Oromo, Sidama, Wolayta and Kaffa lands. The modern borders largely date from these campaigns.

events.title: Adwa
events.description: Menelik's army of about a hundred thousand destroys an Italian force of seventeen thousand. Ethiopia stays independent while the rest of Africa is partitioned, and Adwa becomes a symbol across the continent.

events.title: Lij Iyasu is deposed
events.description: The uncrowned heir is overthrown amid accusations that he had converted to Islam. Zewditu becomes empress with Ras Tafari as regent.

events.title: The railway reaches Addis Ababa
events.description: The French-built line from Djibouti arrives after twenty years, and the capital is linked to the sea.

events.title: Ethiopia joins the League of Nations
events.description: Ras Tafari wins admission on condition that slavery is abolished. The decree comes the next year and enforcement takes decades.

events.title: Haile Selassie is crowned
events.description: Tafari Makonnen takes the throne name Haile Selassie. In Jamaica the coronation is read as prophecy and the Rastafari movement is born.

events.title: The first written constitution
events.description: A constitution creates a parliament with an appointed upper house. It centralises power in the emperor more than it shares it.

events.title: Mussolini invades
events.description: After a border clash at Walwal, Italy attacks from Eritrea and Somalia with aircraft and mustard gas. The League imposes weak sanctions and does nothing else.

events.title: Haile Selassie at Geneva
events.description: The exiled emperor addresses the League in person and is jeered by Italian journalists. "It is us today. It will be you tomorrow."

events.title: Yekatit 12
events.description: After an attempt on the Italian viceroy's life, Blackshirts and settlers massacre Addis Ababa's residents for three days. Monks at Debre Libanos are executed in May.

events.title: Liberation
events.description: British, Commonwealth and Ethiopian forces drive the Italians out, and Haile Selassie re-enters his capital five years to the day after it fell.

events.title: Ethiopian Airlines
events.description: The national carrier begins flying with American help. It becomes the largest and most profitable airline in Africa.

events.title: Ethiopian troops in Korea
events.description: The Kagnew battalion, drawn from the imperial guard, fights with the United Nations command. None of its soldiers is taken prisoner.

events.title: Federation with Eritrea
events.description: The United Nations federates the former Italian colony with Ethiopia under its own constitution.

events.title: A revised constitution
events.description: The emperor grants an elected lower house and universal suffrage, while keeping the power to appoint and dismiss every minister.

events.title: Abebe Bikila wins barefoot in Rome
events.description: A soldier of the imperial guard wins the Olympic marathon barefoot, the first Olympic gold for a black African. He wins again in Tokyo in shoes.

events.title: The coup attempt
events.description: The imperial guard seizes power while the emperor is abroad. It collapses in days, but it is the first open challenge to the throne.

events.title: The Eritrean war begins
events.description: Armed struggle for Eritrean independence starts in the western lowlands, a year before Ethiopia dissolves the federation and annexes Eritrea outright.

events.title: The Organisation of African Unity
events.description: Thirty-two independent African states found the OAU in Addis Ababa, which has been the continent's diplomatic capital since.

events.title: The Wollo famine
events.description: Tens of thousands die in the north while the court hides it. A British documentary contrasting the emperor's banquets with the dying turns opinion in Addis Ababa.

events.title: The Derg deposes the emperor
events.description: A committee of junior officers removes Haile Selassie, who dies in custody a year later. Sixty officials are shot without trial in November.

events.title: Land to the tiller
events.description: All rural land is nationalised and tenancy abolished. It is the most popular thing the Derg ever does.

events.title: The Red Terror
events.description: Mengistu Haile Mariam takes control and wages a campaign against leftist rivals. Tens of thousands are killed and their families billed for the bullets.

events.title: The Ogaden War
events.description: Somalia invades to take the Somali-inhabited east. Soviet and Cuban support switches to Ethiopia and the Somalis are driven back.

events.title: The great famine
events.description: Drought, war and forced resettlement leave perhaps a million dead. Footage from Korem prompts Band Aid and Live Aid.

events.title: Operation Moses
events.description: Israel airlifts about eight thousand Beta Israel, Ethiopian Jews, from Sudanese camps. Operation Solomon flies another 14,000 out in thirty-six hours in 1991.

events.title: The Derg falls
events.description: Tigrayan-led rebels of the EPRDF take Addis Ababa and Mengistu flees to Zimbabwe. Meles Zenawi leads the new government.

events.title: Eritrea becomes independent
events.description: After a referendum with 99.8% in favour, Eritrea separates and Ethiopia becomes landlocked.

events.title: Ethnic federalism
events.description: A new constitution divides the country into regions along ethnic lines and gives each a right to secede.

events.title: War with Eritrea
events.description: A border dispute at Badme becomes a trench war that kills perhaps eighty thousand in two years. A border commission awards Badme to Eritrea and Ethiopia refuses to withdraw.

events.title: The disputed election
events.description: The opposition makes large gains, the government declares victory, and security forces kill about two hundred protesters.

events.title: The Ethiopian millennium
events.description: The Ethiopian calendar, seven to eight years behind the Gregorian, reaches the year 2000. The country celebrates the new millennium seven and a half years after everyone else.

events.title: The Grand Renaissance Dam begun
events.description: Construction starts on the Blue Nile near the Sudanese border, funded largely by Ethiopians themselves. Egypt calls it an existential threat.

events.title: Meles Zenawi dies
events.description: The man who had ruled since 1991 dies in office. Hailemariam Desalegn succeeds him.

events.title: Light rail in Addis Ababa
events.description: Sub-Saharan Africa's first modern light rail opens, built by China, part of a decade of state-led growth near ten per cent a year.

events.title: The Oromo protests
events.description: Protests against the capital's expansion into Oromo farmland spread across the region. Hundreds are killed and a state of emergency is declared.

events.title: Abiy Ahmed takes office
events.description: After years of protest in Oromia and Amhara, a young Oromo officer becomes prime minister, frees political prisoners and makes peace with Eritrea.

events.title: A Nobel Peace Prize
events.description: Abiy is awarded the prize for the settlement with Eritrea. Within a year the country is at war with itself.

events.title: The Tigray war
events.description: Federal and Eritrean forces fight the Tigray People's Liberation Front. Estimates of the dead, from fighting, siege and famine, run to several hundred thousand.

events.title: The Pretoria agreement
events.description: A ceasefire signed in South Africa ends the Tigray war. Fighting continues in Amhara and Oromia.

events.title: Ethiopia joins BRICS
events.description: Ethiopia enters the bloc alongside Egypt, Iran and the UAE, with Africa's second-largest population at about 130 million.
